problem: Black screen / stuck on launch caused by Nahimic audio service (esp. Lenovo laptops) after Vanguard/Valorant update
symptoms: VALORANT opens to a black screen and stays frozen, process uses only ~13-15 MB RAM
Riot client/game stuck after update, friends list missing
Alt+Enter does nothing
root_causes: Nahimic service/driver (an unsigned DLL from a recent Nahimic update on Lenovo laptops) conflicts with Vanguard

fixes.fix: Disable/stop the Nahimic service: Win+R -> services.msc (or msconfig -> Services) -> Nahimic -> Stop and set Disabled / disable at startup; no need to uninstall; restart then launch
Run Riot Client (RiotClientServices.exe) as administrator; this also worked for several Lenovo users
Install FXSound as replacement audio enhancer after disabling Nahimic
Community fix script: github samgeorg777/nahimic-game-crash-fix

diagnostic_signals: Unsigned/blocked Nahimic DLL loaded in VALORANT process
VALORANT process stuck at tiny memory footprint

problem: Run Riot Client as administrator fixes freezes, stutter, FPS drops and black screen after updates
symptoms: Freeze when pressing a keyboard key / in match
Mouse-move FPS drops and stutter after Oct 2026 update
FPS gradually going down (20 fps on homepage)
Black screen on launch
root_causes: Unclear; Vanguard apparently handles non-elevated Riot processes badly (possibly blocked hooks)

fixes.fix: Right-click RiotClientServices.exe (Riot Client root folder, not VALORANT exe) -> Properties -> Compatibility -> Run as administrator; fully close Riot Client incl. tray and relaunch
Run only the Riot Client elevated, not VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe (setting shipping exe to admin does not launch)
Run VALORANT.exe as admin also worked for some
Did not work for everyone (several reported no change)

problem: Stutter / FPS drops / freezes caused by Realtek 2.5GbE Family Controller (often when using Wi-Fi)
symptoms: Periodic micro-freezes every few seconds to 1 minute with audio cuts
Stutter, frame-time spikes, CPU (game) time spikes, ping spikes
Mostly AMD/new high-end PCs (9800X3D, 9070 XT, 7900X, 14700KF)
root_causes: Realtek PCIe/Gaming 2.5GbE controller (rt25cx21 driver) repeatedly throws errors/resets, visible in Event Viewer, interfering with VALORANT

fixes.fix: Device Manager -> Network adapters -> Realtek (Gaming) 2.5GbE Family Controller -> Disable device (only if using Wi-Fi/other NIC); recheck after Windows updates which may re-enable it
Update Realtek 2.5GbE driver from motherboard vendor / BIOS update
Disable Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (Settings > System > Display > Graphics) together with the NIC disable
Disable energy-saving options in NIC device properties (power management/Green Ethernet)
Use a non-Realtek NIC or PCIe Wi-Fi adapter if only Ethernet is available
Did not help in some cases (Wi-Fi-only users still stuttering, disabling gave packet loss for Ethernet users)

diagnostic_signals: Event Viewer errors from rt25cx21 or NIC resets
Whether Ethernet adapter is unused (Wi-Fi connected)

problem: Stutter/FPS drops/loading hangs after Oct 5 2026 patch caused by conflicting third-party software (RTSS/RivaTuner, Premier Opinion, ASUS ScreenXpert, Stardock Fences, GearUP Booster, Huawei PC Manager, MoniVisor)
symptoms: FPS drops from 300+ to 10-80 especially when moving mouse, opening menu, placing smokes, buy phase
Stuck on loading screen
Low client FPS warning
Vanguard CPU use 60-90% at start
Strafe tearing/micro-stutter
Mouse freezes, menu glitches
root_causes: Vanguard now blocks/hostile to hooking monitoring software and unknown DLL injectors; faulting module visible in reliability monitor (perfmon /rel): pmls64.dll (Premier Opinion), RTSSHooks64.dll, AsusWallpaperSettingHook.dll (ASUS ScreenXpert), PerfWndMonModule.dll (Huawei PC Manager)

fixes.fix: Close/uninstall RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS) before playing; MSI Afterburner can stay if all monitoring items are unchecked so RTSS does not autorestart, or add Riot client + VALORANT exes to RTSS exclusions
Uninstall Premier Opinion (pmls64.dll) via Installed apps
Disable ASUS ScreenXpert service in services.msc; also Asus Update/MultiAntenna/Dial/Cert services, AsusMouseAgent, AsusSmartDisplayControl
Uninstall Huawei PC Manager or MoniVisor (C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Assistant App\MV\unins000.exe)

Riot staff list: Rivatuner/RTSS, Stardock, Premier Opinion, ASUS ScreenXpert, GearUP Booster must be disabled/uninstalled; update GPU drivers; add C:\Riot Games and C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard to antivirus exclusions
Clean boot (msconfig, hide Microsoft services, disable third-party services/startup items) then re-enable one by one; find culprit via perfmon /rel faulting module path
Turn off GPU overclock
Set vgc.exe CPU affinity to a single core each launch (Task Manager > Details)

diagnostic_signals: Running processes: RTSS (RTSS.exe, RTSSHooks64.dll), MSI Afterburner, Premier Opinion, Stardock Fences, GearUP Booster, ASUS ScreenXpert/Armoury Crate services, Huawei PC Manager, MoniVisor, SteelSeries/Razer software
Reliability Monitor / Event Viewer crash entries for VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe with faulting module DLL

problem: Shader compilation stutter on UE5/DX11 (no persistent shader cache)
symptoms: Stutter for first minutes after launch, micro-stutter during fights, ability use or skin finishers while FPS counter looks normal
root_causes: Game engine recompiles shaders each launch (DX11 on UE5 cannot persist shader cache) - claimed by commenters

fixes.fix: Use SCSKiller: Library tab -> add game by selecting VALORANT.exe (not Win64-Shipping), clear shader cache, then Compile; author reported smoother frames
Update ethernet and audio drivers
Add RAM / dual-channel (8 GB single channel)
Pre-compile shaders with SCSKiller

diagnostic_signals: Shader cache size in NVIDIA/AMD cache folders

problem: Critical error 'A critical error has occurred and the process must be terminated' due to NVIDIA Vertical sync set to Fast
symptoms: Critical error crash in lobby/after match found, after Sept 2026 update
NVIDIA driver/render errors in logs
root_causes: NVIDIA Control Panel Vertical sync = Fast

fixes.fix: NVIDIA Control Panel -> Manage 3D settings -> Vertical sync: change Fast to 'Use the 3D application setting', apply, relaunch
Same fix confirmed by ~8 commenters (also resetting 3D settings)
Clean reinstall of both dGPU and iGPU drivers (iGPU reinstall stopped crashes for one commenter)
Roll back NVIDIA driver (to July version) plus run Riot Client as admin

diagnostic_signals: NVIDIA Control Panel vsync mode Fast
GPU driver errors in Event Viewer

problem: VAN 9001/9003 and Restriction errors: TPM 2.0 / Secure Boot requirement unmet
symptoms: Vanguard kicks player with TPM 2.0 / Secure Boot errors
Windows 10 on old hardware without TPM 2.0
root_causes: No TPM 2.0 on board (X99, H61, TPM 1.2 laptops) or Secure Boot disabled/misconfigured
Account flagged as suspicious so TPM requirement is enforced even on Windows 10

fixes.fix: Add a TPM 2.0 module on motherboard header (e.g. JLPC1 on Huananzhi X99), enable Security Device Support, set CSM Disabled/UEFI, delete Secure Boot variables, enroll factory default keys, enable Secure Boot; verify tpm.msc ready and msinfo32 Secure Boot State On; full shutdown if TPM not detected
If hardware has only TPM 1.2/no TPM and account is flagged, only options are another account or new hardware; update BIOS first
Update to latest BIOS

diagnostic_signals: Get-Tpm / tpm.msc: TPM present, version 2.0, ready
msinfo32 BIOS mode UEFI, Secure Boot State
Disk partition style GPT vs MBR

problem: Secure Boot violation boot loop after enabling Secure Boot / default keys
symptoms: Red 'Secure Boot Violation - unauthorized changes' panel at boot after installing default keys
root_causes: Corrupted EFI boot files / key enrollment mismatch on ASUS ROG Z270

fixes.fix: In BIOS set OS type from Windows UEFI to 'Other OS', clear Secure Boot keys, save; then in Windows run admin cmd to rebuild EFI boot files; afterwards Secure Boot State shows On in msinfo32

problem: Memory integrity / IOMMU / UEFI toggle causes black screen or stuck at logo on boot
symptoms: Black screen or stuck at ASUS logo after enabling memory integrity; BIOS save then black screen on boot (IOMMU/UEFI)
root_causes: Unknown; BIOS/UEFI mode or partition style conflict (suggested GPT vs MBR, hypervisor setting)

fixes.fix: Reset the PC (Windows reset)
bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off and verify disk is GPT

problem: Valorant says Windows 10 version is too old
symptoms: Vanguard demands higher Windows 10 version; winver shows 1909
root_causes: Outdated Windows build and Windows Update unable to upgrade

fixes.fix: Download the Windows ISO from Microsoft site, mount it and run setup to upgrade; check winver afterwards

problem: High ping / packet loss from ISP routing to Riot servers (Florida/Georgia, Jakarta, Cape Town, Riyadh)
symptoms: Ping doubled (e.g. 21 to 53 ms) on usual region, packet loss to GA/VA/IL servers
Ping stuck near 90 despite fast internet
root_causes: ISP routing issues / regional outages (undersea cable cuts), not local hardware

fixes.fix: Use Cloudflare WARP (1.1.1.1 client, no account) connected before launching game; took ping from 72 to 35 ms
Contact ISP; test on another connection (OP in Jakarta found their ISP was the cause)
Use LAN cable, avoid 2.4GHz Wi-Fi
Open Riot support ticket and run ping tester

problem: In-game voice chat not working (X on icons, no team voice) fixed by changing DNS / using Cloudflare WARP
symptoms: Voice chat icons marked with X; can hear self in loopback but not others in match; volume sliders missing
root_causes: ISP DNS / IPv6 routing preventing Riot voice server connection

fixes.fix: Change to public DNS (Google 8.8.8.8 or Cloudflare 1.1.1.1); one reported it lasted only ~3 days because ISP reset it
Cloudflare WARP fixed voice chat (slightly higher ping)
Disable/re-enable ethernet adapter mid game

problem: Stuck on loading screen (no error) caused by VPN, antivirus or disabled Hyper-V platform features
symptoms: VALORANT stuck at loading screen forever with vgc running
stuck in Riot client after update
root_causes: VPN software interfering
Antivirus blocking
Windows optional features Virtual Machine Platform / Hypervisor Platform disabled

fixes.fix: Win+R optionalfeatures -> enable 'Virtual Machine Platform' and 'Windows Hypervisor Platform', OK, restart
Disable/uninstall VPNs (found with AI-assisted diagnosis)
Temporarily disable Windows antivirus while playing
Add Riot/Vanguard folders to AV exclusions

diagnostic_signals: VirtualMachinePlatform and HypervisorPlatform optional feature state

problem: VALORANT shows offline / greyed Play button due to incorrect Windows date and time
symptoms: Riot Client shows VALORANT offline, Play button greyed out, repair does nothing
Logs: 'SSL certificate problem: certificate is not yet valid', 'Dependency DirectX failed to install'
root_causes: System clock wrong so SSL certificate validation fails to Riot CDN

fixes.fix: Correct Windows date/time and sync time (ReviOS install had wrong clock)

problem: 'VALORANT Failed To Launch - Something unusual happened' fixed by accepting Terms and Conditions popup
symptoms: Failed to launch error even after reinstall/regedit tweaks; terms popup never shown
root_causes: Terms and Conditions not accepted in Riot Client

fixes.fix: Log out and back into Riot Client to trigger the terms and conditions popup and accept

problem: Game runs on integrated GPU / dedicated GPU not detected; or freezes at start until iGPU adapter enabled
symptoms: Freezes on loading, stuck in windowed mode, Multithreaded Rendering option missing
Error: D3D11-compatible GPU required when iGPU disabled
Game freezes on start/within a minute on new AMD build
root_causes: Game selected iGPU, dedicated GPU not seen; or AMD Radeon Graphics iGPU adapter disabled in Device Manager

fixes.fix: Install older NVIDIA driver and adjust NVIDIA app settings (1100 fps afterwards)
Enable the 'AMD Radeon Graphics' (iGPU) display adapter in Device Manager
Set preferred GPU for VALORANT in Windows Graphics settings / NVIDIA control panel

diagnostic_signals: Display adapters in Device Manager and enabled state

problem: Windows environment variables missing breaks Vanguard log export ('Failed to create zip archive')
symptoms: Vanguard tray panel 'Save logs' fails with Failed to create zip archive in any folder
root_causes: Basic Windows system environment variables missing

fixes.fix: Restore missing system environment variables (System Properties > Environment Variables), reboot

diagnostic_signals: Presence of standard env vars (TEMP, SystemRoot, etc.)

problem: TPM event 17/14 freezes and VAN 9001 hang in menu - VGC service not running
symptoms: Game freezes 20 s into menu then critical error; TPM Event 17/14 in Event Viewer; PC hard freeze
root_causes: vgc service on Manual and not running; chipset driver outdated

fixes.fix: services.msc -> vgc -> Startup type Automatic and Start the service, then launch VALORANT
Update chipset driver and set vgc to automatic
Update BIOS, clear TPM (did not fix for OP)

diagnostic_signals: vgc service status and start type

problem: VAN 185 returning after setting VALORANT/Discord priority to High
symptoms: Recurring VAN 185 despite DNS flush, Vanguard reinstall, VGC restart
root_causes: VALORANT and Discord process priority set to High/Realtime on low-end PC (Task Manager or Process Lasso)

fixes.fix: Set VALORANT and Discord priority back to Above normal (avoid High/Realtime)

diagnostic_signals: Process priority class of VALORANT and Discord

problem: VAN 136 / Vanguard high CPU usage on very old hardware
symptoms: Vanguard uses more CPU/RAM than the game, queue dodges, FPS drops
Vanguard 30% CPU after motherboard swap
root_causes: Weak CPU (i5-5300U); unknown for motherboard swap case

fixes.fix: Hardware upgrade (OP agreed); reinstalling Vanguard did not work
Fresh Windows installs did not fix (B550M case)

problem: Disable multi-plane overlay / overlays fixes fullscreen flicker on AMD

root_causes: Multi-plane overlay / driver overlays

root_causes: Unconfirmed: drivers, HAGS, AMD overlay

Switching Windows version (11 to 10 worked for another user)

root_causes: Unknown client bug
